factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Shut down, sleep, or hibernate your PC
factual_notes.note: Microsoft documents the power-button and laptop lid actions, notes that wake methods vary by PC, and describes hibernate as using less power than sleep but resuming more slowly.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Change the power mode for your Windows PC
factual_notes.note: Windows 11 exposes power mode under Settings > System > Power & battery; custom power plans can affect which options are available.

powercfg /a reports available sleep states, /requests lists application and driver power requests, /lastwake reports the last wake source, /waketimers lists active wake timers, and /devicequery wake_armed lists devices configured to wake the PC.
Power requests can prevent display power-off or low-power sleep; systemsleepdiagnostics generates a recent sleep-transition report and requires elevation.
Windows sleep behavior depends on the sleep states implemented by the hardware. Microsoft directs users to powercfg /a to enumerate the states available on a specific PC.
Modern Standby distinguishes Screen Off and Sleep segments; screen-off activity does not by itself prove that the system has reached its lowest-power sleep phase.
SleepStudy is an inbox report for Modern Standby PCs. It summarizes Active, Screen Off, and Sleep periods and identifies top activity sources without acting as an automatic repair tool.
The current dashboard was opened on 2026-08-04 and provides separate known-issue pages for Windows 11 versions 26H1, 25H2, and 24H2.

The current message center was opened for time-sensitive update context. It includes narrow device and driver notices, so an entry must match the reader's Windows version, update, model, and symptom before it is treated as relevant.

topic_context.difference_from_existing: This article separates automatic-timer failure, failed sleep entry, immediate wake, and missing sleep states, then uses power-request and wake-source evidence; the existing battery article focuses on battery drain rather than failure to sleep.
